title: Wonunke (Westhampton)
summary: Wonunke is a Westhampton placename for necks of land east of Beaver Dam River, later appearing in Great and Little Wonunk forms.
map_geometry_source: USGS Eastport quadrangle (2010), Oneck label; Tooker (1911), pp. 290–291, Onuck/Wonunke. Approximate modern neighborhood anchor, not an exact historical boundary.
introduction_content: Wonunke belongs to the named necks east of Beaverdam River in Westhampton. The forms Great Wonunk, Little Wonunk and later Onuck record distinctions within that coastal landscape, rather than a single isolated landmark. Tooker, pp. 290–291
history_content:
The 1681 meadow allotment lists Ononke alongside Assops, Ketchaponack and Potunk. In 1686, the town described Wonunk through a footpath, a creek crossing from Potunk and water on its western side. These relational descriptions are more informative than placing the name at an arbitrary point beside Quantuck. Tooker, pp. 290–291

The 1686 town-book descriptions can be read together to compare the neighboring necks, waterways and crossings. Southampton town records, vol. II, printed pp. 113–114
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as "the bend," referring to a bend of land or water.

Why Place Names Matter

“Beyond the practical function they serve, Indigenous place names recount stories of the land in a unique way and provide valuable cultural and historical perspectives.”

— Translation Bureau, Government of Canada, Indigenous geographical names and the power they hold (2019), Language Portal of Canada blog, section “The moose that jumped over the rapids”
preservation_content: Wonunke connects modern Westhampton shoreline geography with older Southampton records and Indigenous-language place naming. The historic neck boundaries remain uncertain.
whereintheworld_content:
The pin indicates the broader Oneck area west of Moneyboque Bay in present-day Westhampton Beach. Tooker records Onuck among the later forms of Wonunke and describes the necks east of Beaverdam/Apocock. The USGS Eastport map labels Oneck and Oneck Drain in this landscape, providing a better modern reference than the Quantuck shoreline farther east. Tooker, pp. 290–291 Eastport, New York — US Topo map

The point is an approximate neighborhood reference, not a particular home, an exact Native settlement location, or the boundary of Great or Little Wonunk. The historical creek crossings and neck limits remain uncertain, so no land polygon is drawn.
